thag7.1:1.1: The courtesan (_vesikā_) here is depicted as refined and cultured, deploying customary niceties and playful allusions as artfully as she does her carefully groomed appearance. Kauṭilya (Arthaśāstra 2.27) recommends that kings should sponsor the education of courtesans in “singing; playing musical instruments; reciting; dancing; acting; writing; painting; playing the lute, ﬂute, and drum; reading another’s mind (_paracittajñāna_); preparing perfumes and garlands; conversation; shampooing; and the arts of a courtesan” (see note on [an3.39:2.2]()). This discourse gives us an idea how those arts might be deployed on that most difficult of targets, a confirmed renunciate.
thag7.1:2.1: An indication of submission, in contrast with the haughty behavior of the brahmin lady of the Verahaccāni clan ([sn35.133:2.7]()).
thag7.1:2.2: In the Suttas, this gesture is only used in honor of esteemed spiritual masters.
thag7.1:3.1: She is familiar with the Vedic custom whereby a man goes forth only in the last stage of life. Rather than trying to make him abandon his spiritual quest, she urges that life with her would be fulfilling the proper stages of life.
thag7.1:3.2: She plays with the word _sāsana_, normally used for a religious “dispensation”. Her method is to beguile by offering shifting perspectives: she is dressed seductively, then removes her sandals; she offers submission, then acts like a spiritual teacher.
thag7.1:3.4: While obviously a pun, a courtesan could become a wealthy woman ([dn16:2.14.1]()). Again, she inverts expectations; normally the man would have been expected to provide income.
thag7.1:3.5: She pledges on the sacred power of the truth, again inverting the misogynistic belief that a woman can never be trusted ([an5.230:2.9]()).
thag7.1:3.6: She is well aware of the Vedic notion that a woman, specifically her vagina, is the “fire” into which the Soma offering of semen is made (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 6.4.3, 6.4.12, 6.2.22). | For _harāmi_, compare [snp2.1:2.3](), where the _bali_ offerings are “brought”.
